title: Phase 2: Benchmark reference table + CPU-name matching/override system + unmatched-CPU reporting
description:
Delivers: the benchmark-map/ artifact -- PassMark reference table, alias table, manual override list -- plus the pipeline logic that generates the unmatched-CPU report (unmatched-cpus.json) each run.

Completion criteria:
- The CPU-matching fixture set (Testing Strategy) resolves correctly against the reference/alias tables
- An intentionally-unmatchable CPU string produces benchmark_matched = false, never a guessed score
- Near-miss adversarial pairs (Testing Strategy category 3) each resolve to their own correct match and are asserted to never cross-match each other -- this is the fixture set's only defense against Risk Register R1
- Unmatched-CPU report is generated in the unmatched-cpus.json shape and lists every unresolved CPU seen in the fixture set -- publishing it to R2 happens in Phase 4

See docs/plan/plan.md Implementation Phases.

title: User-selectable primary sort axis (RAM/disk-first mode)
description: Let RAM- or storage-heavy buyers (NAS, in-memory cache workloads) promote price_per_gb_ram or price_per_tb_disk to the primary sort instead of price_per_benchmark_point_multi. Direct extension of ADR-3's 'separate metrics, user decides priority' philosophy -- benchmark-value stays the documented default, this is opt-in. From idea-gen run 2026-08-02, ledger finalist #2. v1.1 tier.

title: Genesis: hetzner-auction-dashboard Implementation
description:
## Genesis Bead
Tied to plan: docs/plan/plan.md

## Overview
Client-side dashboard for Hetzner server auction listings. A pipeline joins CPU benchmark scores onto listings and publishes a Parquet file (plus a companion unmatched-CPU report) to Cloudflare R2 via a temp-key-then-swap lifecycle; a static browser frontend on Cloudflare Pages using DuckDB-WASM does search/filter/sort only. The benchmark join itself is the core differentiator.

## Progress
- [ ] Phase 1: Pipeline -- fetch Hetzner auction data, define raw schema
- [ ] Phase 2: Benchmark reference table + CPU-name matching/override system + unmatched-CPU reporting
- [ ] Phase 3: Cost-metric computation + Parquet writer
- [ ] Phase 4: R2 bucket + API token + refresh-loop Deployment via declarative-config
- [ ] Phase 5: Client dashboard -- DuckDB-WASM wiring + search/filter UI
- [ ] Phase 6: Deploy pipeline to a Rackspace Spot cluster via GitOps; wire up Cloudflare Pages for web/

v1.1 additions (had-4ct, had-1vp, had-33l, had-39b, had-2ua) and v2/Future Candidates are tracked separately and do not block this genesis bead -- they are explicitly non-blocking per the plan.

title: Phase 1: Pipeline -- fetch Hetzner auction data, define raw schema
description:
Delivers: a working fetcher against Hetzner's live auction feed and a defined raw schema for what a listing looks like before any enrichment.

Completion criteria:
- Fetcher successfully retrieves and parses a real auction response end-to-end
- Raw schema fields match Data Models' pre-enrichment columns (listing_id, cpu_raw, ram_gb, disks, price_base, etc.)
- A malformed/empty response is handled without crashing (see Edge Case Catalog EC-1/EC-2)

See docs/plan/plan.md Implementation Phases.

title: Saved/named filter presets (URL-encoded)
description: Serialize current filter state into URL query params on every filter change, read back on page load -- bookmarkable, no sharing required, pure self-bookmarking for the one real user. From idea-gen run 2026-08-02, ledger finalist #5. v1.1 tier -- user explicitly deprioritized this behind core v1 functionality, hence Low priority.

title: Diff view between two Parquet snapshots
description: Client-side (IndexedDB) comparison of 'what changed since I last looked' -- cache the previous fetched snapshot and diff row-by-config-signature against the current one. Gets partial price-history value weeks before v2's full historical-stats architecture ships, with zero pipeline changes. From idea-gen run 2026-08-02, ledger finalist #3. v1.1 tier.

title: Cross-link listings to Hetzner's own Cloud catalog pricing
description: Show 'X% cheaper than the equivalent still-selling Hetzner Cloud instance' on each listing. Requires a small, separately hand-maintained lookup table mapping common CPU/RAM/disk tiers to their nearest Hetzner Cloud SKU price (catalog pricing changes rarely, unlike the 10-min auction feed, so maintenance burden is low). From idea-gen run 2026-08-02, ledger finalist #4. v1.1 tier -- note in Components as a small new lookup artifact, distinct from benchmark-map/.

title: Starter-configs + one-click best-deal button
description: Pre-built example searches (e.g. Budget web server, Home NAS, Game server) as one-click filter presets, plus a single 'best deal now' button returning one defensible top-value listing (highest price_per_benchmark_point_multi, benchmark_matched=true). For a first-time visitor who doesn't want to configure filters at all. From idea-gen run 2026-08-02, docs/notes/ideas-ledger.md finalist #1. v1.1 tier — not blocking Phase 5's core filter/sort scope.

title: Phase 4: R2 bucket + API token + refresh-loop Deployment via declarative-config
description:
Delivers: a running pipeline Deployment (replicas: 1, GitOps-managed) that fetches, computes, and publishes to R2 on the 10-minute cadence using the full temp-key-then-swap lifecycle.

Completion criteria:
- Deployment reconciles cleanly via ArgoCD from declarative-config
- R2 API token stored as an ExternalSecret, never appears in pipeline logs
- A forced failure mid-run leaves both live R2 keys untouched (Parquet snapshot + unmatched-cpus.json), each independently verified by hash before/after
- Both artifacts publish to R2 each cycle via the temp-key-then-swap lifecycle with Cache-Control: max-age=60 applied

See docs/plan/plan.md Implementation Phases.

title: Phase 5: Client dashboard -- DuckDB-WASM wiring + search/filter UI
description:
Delivers: the static web/ site that loads the published Parquet file via DuckDB-WASM httpfs and implements all Client Dashboard Scope (v1) filters/sorts.

Completion criteria:
- Dashboard loads a real published snapshot, correct filtered/sorted results for each filter type in scope
- Default sort is price_per_benchmark_point_multi ascending, NULLS FIRST; unscored listings visibly flagged and grouped at the top
- A simulated load failure (bad URL) shows the Graceful Degradation error state, not a blank page
- Early in this phase: confirm agentation actually publishes a CDN-consumable ESM build (ADR-5's invalidation trigger) before proceeding further
- Agentation's toolbar is mounted via the isolated React root (ADR-5) and functions independently of the dashboard

See docs/plan/plan.md Implementation Phases.

title: Phase 6: Deploy pipeline to a Rackspace Spot cluster via GitOps; wire up Cloudflare Pages for web/
description:
Delivers: both halves live in production -- pipeline running unattended on its chosen cluster, web/ served from Cloudflare Pages against the real R2 bucket.

Completion criteria:
- Pipeline completes at least 3 consecutive scheduled runs without manual intervention
- Cloudflare Pages deployment serves the dashboard and successfully loads the live Parquet file end-to-end
- Open Questions' cluster choice is resolved and reflected in declarative-config

See docs/plan/plan.md Implementation Phases.

title: Phase 3: Cost-metric computation + Parquet writer
description:
Delivers: price_effective_monthly, price_per_benchmark_point_single, price_per_benchmark_point_multi, price_per_gb_ram, and price_per_tb_disk computed per listing, written to a single flat Parquet file.

Completion criteria:
- price_effective_monthly computes correctly against a fixture set, including one listing with non-zero price_setup_fee and one with zero
- All four per-resource metrics compute correctly against a fixture set, including one with benchmark_matched = false (NULL, never divide-by-zero)
- Parquet writer's output passes the DuckDB-WASM httpfs conformance test (Testing Strategy) -- required for Phase 3 completion since Phase 4/5 both build on this file format

See docs/plan/plan.md Implementation Phases.
